American actor Stacy Keach, known for playing Mike Hammer and Ernest Hemingway, dead at 85

The stage and screen actor who became known for playing private investigator Mike Hammer on television died on Tuesday (Nov 10).

FAST

Actor Stacy Keach, who portrayed rugged characters such as fictional detective Mike Hammer and legendary American novelist Ernest Hemingway, died on Tuesday (Nov 10) at the age of 85, his wife said in a statement to Hollywood trade publication Variety. Keach died in Poland "after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure", his wife, actress Malgosia Tomassi, said in the statement. “Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family,” Tomassi added. Keach stood out in dozens of starring and character actor parts on television and in films in roles as diverse as Barabbas in the television miniseries Jesus Of Nazareth and Richard Nixon in the play Frost/Nixon.  He also had a busy stage career, often starring in Shakespearean works such as King Lear and Hamlet. His performance as the latter in 1972 inspired a New York Times critic to label Keach "the finest American classic actor since John Barrymore".

FILE PHOTO: 71st Cannes Film Festival - Photocall for the film Gotti - Cannes, France, May 15, 2018. Cast member Stacy Keach. REUTERS/Regis Duvignau/File Photo

Keach's most prominent role was Mike Hammer, the hard-boiled detective, clad in a fedora and trench coat, in television adaptations of the works of suspense writer Mickey Spillane.  The New Mike Hammer ran from the mid to late 1980s, and Keach revived the character in the Mike Hammer, Private Eye series from 1997 to 1998. He also played Hammer in four made-for-television movies and narrated audio versions of Spillane's books. "I have been and always shall be Mike Hammer," Keach wrote in his 2013 autobiography, All In All: An Actor's Life On And Off The Stage. He added: "Certain roles stick to you, and I'm happy that Hammer is mine." The first Hammer series was interrupted when Keach went to prison for six months in England in 1985 after more than 30 grams of cocaine was found in his possessions at London's Heathrow Airport. In his book, he said he had been addicted, and in 2013 Keach told Fox News that getting caught "saved my life, actually". Keach also had a history with Hemingway, the complex Nobel Prize-winning author and adventurer. His portrayal of the writer in Hemingway in the 1988 television miniseries earned him a Golden Globe award and an Emmy nomination.   Keach was born Jun 2, 1941, in Savannah, Georgia, and grew up in Southern California. As a child, he underwent several surgeries for a cleft lip and cleft palate. "Only when I was maligned and teased by kids did it bother me," Keach told Fox News. "I became an overachiever as a result of that. I had to excel in sports to make up for that. It was a motor. It gave me an incentive to do better."     For some roles, the scar on his lip was concealed by a moustache, but in a 2016 interview with the Cleft Palate Foundation, Keach said he preferred to let it show when he was in a tough-guy role, such as a mobster, or playing a vulnerable character. Keach's father, Stacy Sr, was a director and actor who worked steadily in television from the 1950s through the '80s. His brother James Keach was also an actor. Keach graduated from the University of California at Berkeley and also studied at the Yale School of Drama and was a Fulbright Scholar at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art. In the foreword of All In All, actor Alec Baldwin described Keach as "a miraculous hybrid of the hyper-masculinity of a Brando or Robert Mitchum and the classical training of Richard Burton or Kevin Kline". Keach's movie work included John Huston's Fat City, The New Centurions, The Life And Times Of Judge Roy Bean, American History X, The Long Riders with his brother, That Championship Season, and the Cheech and Chong comedies Up In Smoke and Nice Dreams. His regular television roles included Titus, Prison Break and Two And A Half Men. On Broadway, he starred in Other Desert Cities in 2011 to 2012, The Kentucky Cycle and Solitary Confinement in the 1990s and Deathtrap in the 1970s. Keach suffered an apparent heart attack on stage in May 2017 on opening night of Pamplona, a one-man play about Hemingway in his later years, which forced the cancellation of the show's run. He also suffered a mild stroke in 2009 during a run of Frost/Nixon but returned to the stage 10 days later.  Keach is survived by Tomassi, a Polish-born actress who appeared with him in various Hammer shows. He was married three times previously and had a years-long relationship with singer Judy Collins in the 1970s.

Source: Reuters/iz

DUBAI: Tehran has designated Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organisations", Iran's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday (Nov 11), in a reciprocal move following Buenos Aires' designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards as a terrorist entity in April.  Argentina had designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation, following a push from US President Donald Trump's administration for allies to do so.  Iran's Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday that Tehran considers the Argentinian air force and navy terrorist organisations "based on the principle of reciprocity".  "It is evident that the responsibility for all consequences arising from this matter will lie with the Argentine government," the ministry added, without elaborating. It made no mention of Argentina's army. Argentina said in April that the measure it took against Iran's IRGC was due to its backing for Lebanon-based Hezbollah, which Buenos Aires blames for the deadliest bombing in the South American nation's history, a 1994 attack on the AMIA Jewish community centre in the Argentinian capital that killed 85 and injured hundreds. The IRGC is an elite military force that protects Shi'ite Muslim clerical rule in Iran and controls large parts of Iran's economy.

Source: Reuters/ec

TOKYO, Nov 11 : Japan's largest oil refiner Eneos Holdings raised its fiscal 2026 net profit forecast on Wednesday by 48 per cent to 615 billion yen ($3.87 billion), citing stronger-than-expected oil prices, despite a hefty impairment on renewable energy assets. • The company said it now expects net profit for the year ending March 2027 to rise from its May prediction of 415 billion yen, driven by higher crude oil prices and stronger overseas petroleum product prices • Eneos booked a 111.8 billion yen impairment loss in the July-September second quarter on its renewable energy business, primarily related to goodwill from its 2022 acquisition of Japan Renewable Energy • For the April-September first half of fiscal 2026, net profit jumped nearly eightfold from a year earlier to 511.9 billion yen ($1 = 158.7600 yen)

WASHINGTON: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently moved from his Washington, DC residence to a US military base after Iranian threats against his life, two people familiar with the matter said on Tuesday (Nov 10). The New York Times first reported the move. A senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month that Iranian plots against US personnel and American citizens had reached an advanced stage. Bessent has led the US sanctions and economic pressure campaign against Iran, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, since August to try to push Tehran to end attacks on shipping and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The crucial waterway has been largely closed since the US and Israel attacked Iran on Feb 28. The economic pressure campaign, which coincides with a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, has included sanctions on Middle Eastern bank branches and other financial services firms facilitating transactions with Iran.

"The secretary will not be deterred by the Iranian regime's threats and remains committed to executing Operation Economic Outcast and maintaining the blockade, which together are collapsing Iran's economy," a US Treasury spokesperson said in an emailed statement. The Times reported the severity of the threats to Bessent was not immediately clear. A source familiar with the matter said security concerns surrounding Bessent increased when the Wall Street Journal published an aerial view of the Georgetown mansion that Bessent bought for US$12.5 million shortly after his confirmation as Treasury secretary in January 2025. The photo allowed Bessent's home to be geolocated, and Bessent was relocated to a military base for his safety, the source said, adding: "The news media has an obligation to act responsibly amid growing threats against public officials." Iran has previously denied plotting to attack officials and people on US soil. The New York Times reported that US officials have noted that Iran's ability to carry out large-scale attacks in the US and other territories overseas is limited. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon during the war have killed thousands and displaced millions. American and Israeli attacks have also killed top Iranian officials, including late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Top US business leaders, including Tesla chief Elon Musk, are expected to join President Donald Trump's delegation to China for next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit , the South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported on Tuesday (Nov 10), although it said Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's attendance is uncertain. Huang had previously been in talks to join the delegation, but his participation is now in doubt, the report said, citing sources, amid a recent controversy that has prompted Nvidia's board to investigate whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The APEC summit is set for November 18-19 in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.

Nov 11 : Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha said Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or victory can inspire a new generation of English footballers, including himself, to follow in the Bayern Munich striker's footsteps and be recognised as the world's best. Kane was awarded football's highest individual honour last month, becoming the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. "Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or is definitely a big thing," the 18-year-old told British media.

SEOUL: South Korea's Fair Trade Commission said on Wednesday (Nov 11) that the regulator levied fines totalling 1.6 trillion won (US$1.2 billion) on 15 domestic brokerage firms and banks for colluding at government bond auctions for more than three years. The regulator said that from January 2020 to June 2023, the 15 primary dealers exchanged information by phone or the Telegram messaging app on their bidding yields one or two minutes before the deadlines in 150 government bond auctions. In 145 of those auctions, they directly agreed on bidding yields and volumes, the commission said. Such activities resulted in an artificial rise in South Korean bond yields, the FTC said. The FTC said it expects the penalty to foster effective competition in bond auctions and increase the efficiency of national fiscal management.

Source: Reuters/ec

Nov 11 : The second match in the two-test series between Pakistan and Sri Lanka next week has been moved to Rawalpindi from Lahore due to worsening smog, the Pakistan Cricket Board said on Tuesday. Rawalpindi is currently hosting the series opener, with the second match to be played from November 17-21 as scheduled. Lahore has been grappling with poor air quality in recent weeks as seasonal smog blankets large parts of Pakistan during the winter months. According to IQAir, a Swiss air-quality monitoring company, Lahore is currently the most polluted major city in the world. Air-quality concerns have disrupted cricket schedules in Pakistan before. Smog led to the relocation of a limited-overs series against Zimbabwe from Lahore to Rawalpindi in 2020, and a test against New Zealand from Multan to Karachi in 2022.

Source: Reuters

MELBOURNE, Nov 11 : Usman Khawaja has cancelled events to promote his new book, local media reported on Wednesday, after an awkward TV interview in which he refused to confirm whether Australia's bowlers were involved in the 2018 ball-tampering plot in South Africa. Batsmen Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were sanctioned over the 'Sandpapergate' scandal, but Khawaja said in his autobiography 'Sabr' that knowledge of the plan to manipulate the ball was not confined to those three players and that the whole team should be held responsible. Cricket Australia (CA) CEO Todd Greenberg has ruled out another investigation into the scandal, but pressure was growing on Wednesday for the governing body to reopen the case. Appearing on the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's "7:30" programme on Tuesday, Khawaja was asked whether captain Pat Cummins and his fellow bowlers had prior knowledge that sandpaper was being used to change the condition of the ball.

"You've got to remember Pat Cummins is a good friend of mine, Mitchell Starc, a lot of these guys, guys on the team, other players on the team," he replied. "Shaun Marsh, Mitch Marsh, all very good friends of mine. "I'm not here to go on a witch hunt, all I've ever wanted is for us to take accountability as a team and I don't think that's a lot to say." Fast bowler Starc denied prior knowledge of the ball-tampering on Tuesday. Warner, who was banned from the team for a year and cast by Cricket Australia's investigation as the chief architect of the plot, threw his weight behind Khawaja on Monday and said his account was 100 per cent accurate.  Cummins said in South Africa last month that he had spoken to Khawaja about his book and was not concerned about any potential fallout. “He just basically gave me the heads-up that he's doing a book, and yeah, as always, no worries. Tell your story. It's fine,” Cummins said. Khawaja said in the interview he hoped other teammates would come forward and talk about the 2018 saga honestly but he was not forcing anyone to do anything, nor calling on CA to re-investigate. "I'm not calling for anything, I'm literally sharing my version of the truth," he added. Australian media reported Khawaja pulled out of TV and radio interviews to promote his book following the TV interview. Khawaja and his book's publisher Penguin did not provide an immediate response to requests for comment. While Greenberg said on Tuesday there was "no compelling reason" for another investigation, there have been growing calls for CA to take another look at the scandal. Editorials in two major newspapers have called on CA to take action while The Australian newspaper urged Cummins to break his silence as the team's captain. Simon Longstaff, who led a cultural investigation into Australian cricket in the wake of 'Sandpapergate', said Khawaja and Warner's allegations had shone a spotlight into the darker corners of the men's game. "My fear is that if the belatedly revealed claims are proven true, the damage to the game will be at least as great as that caused by the original sin of ball tampering," he wrote in a column in the Australian Financial Review.

Source: Reuters
